aboutH2: Village of Hope: Faith-Based Residential Recovery in Upper Tracy, New Brunswick
intro: Village of Hope is a Non-Profit rehab located in Tracy, New Brunswick. Village of Hope specializes in the treatment of substance, drug and alcohol abuse.

It is a Christian program, and it says so plainly. Adult men and women live on the campus for 10 months, and the time is split between faith, counselling, work and repairing family ties. Two pastors started it in 2008, and the registered charity behind it is funded by donations.

pillars.title: A Rural Campus on Back Tracy Road
pillars.body: The campus is at 1100 Back Tracy Road in Upper Tracy, on the North Branch of the Oromocto River and about 45 minutes south of Fredericton. A news report on its expansion put the site at 350 acres. The main building is a timber-framed lodge, and residents sleep in shared rooms with shared bathrooms. In late winter the residents tap the maple trees on the property, and the centre holds a Maple Fest in early March. The province has committed $1.46 million for a women's dormitory and a visitors and families centre, which will add a children's play area, classrooms, an industrial kitchen and a multi-purpose hall.

pillars.title: Families Are Brought Into the Program
pillars.body: Rebuilding family relationships is one of the stated goals. About three weeks in, residents can start having visitors on Sundays from 2 to 5 pm, once each visitor has attended an orientation class. During visits, families can join Family Recovery, a 9-week course they take together with the residents. For life after the program, the centre talks about accountability partners and lasting connections with the community rather than a set aftercare schedule, so ask what support continues once the 10 months are over.

pillars.title: Started by Two Pastors in 2008
pillars.body: Pastors Andrew and Märt Vähi founded Village of Hope in 2008, and Andrew Vähi is its executive director. The program is openly Christian. The first phase, about four weeks long, introduces Christianity and Christian living, and the weeks that follow mix devotions, worship and biblical counselling with group therapy, counselling and trauma work. Some of the people running the program came through it themselves: in a 2017 CBC story the program leader was a graduate. A sister Village of Hope operates independently in Estonia.

overview: Village of Hope runs one program: a 10-month residential stay for adults with drug or alcohol problems, built on Christian faith. Recovery.com lists residential care only, with no detox, outpatient or virtual options. The days combine spiritual practice with counselling, group therapy, physical work and training in skills such as budgeting and handling conflict.

afterOverview: The work is part of the treatment. Residents keep up daily responsibilities, take part in the work program and learn employment skills, which the centre sees as the way to build a steady work ethic. Village of Hope accepts people from across Canada. Anyone who needs medical withdrawal management should arrange it before arriving, because detox is not offered on site.

location.intro: Village of Hope is on Back Tracy Road in Upper Tracy, a rural area off Route 101 about 45 minutes south of Fredericton and roughly 40 minutes from Oromocto. From Saint John the drive takes about an hour and a quarter, and from Moncton about two and a half hours.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its public profiles. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Village of Hope cost?
faqs.a: Recovery.com lists a $1,000 entrance fee for the 10-month program, and no other fees are published. Village of Hope is a registered charity that runs on donations. Call the office to confirm the current fee and what it covers before you plan.

faqs.q: How long is the program at Village of Hope?
faqs.a: The program runs for 10 months. The first phase lasts about four weeks and introduces the program along with Christianity and Christian living. The rest of the stay combines counselling, group therapy, work and family sessions.

faqs.q: Is Village of Hope a Christian program?
faqs.a: Yes. Village of Hope describes itself as a faith-based program, and Christian teaching runs through the whole stay. The schedule includes daily devotions, worship, prayer and biblical counselling, alongside group therapy and professional counselling. It was founded in 2008 by two pastors.

faqs.q: Who can attend Village of Hope?
faqs.a: The program is for adult men and women with drug or alcohol problems, and it is run as a co-ed residential program. The centre accepts people from across Canada. With provincial funding, it is also adding a women's dormitory and a visitors and families centre.

faqs.q: Does Village of Hope offer detox?
faqs.a: No. Recovery.com lists detox as not offered, so the centre does not provide medical withdrawal management. If you need supervised withdrawal, arrange it through your doctor or a withdrawal management service before you arrive, and ask the office how they handle the timing.

faqs.q: Where is Village of Hope and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Village of Hope is at 1100 Back Tracy Road in Upper Tracy, New Brunswick, about 45 minutes south of Fredericton by car. Saint John is about an hour and a quarter away and Moncton about two and a half hours. Call the office before you travel.

Yes, once you are about three weeks into the program. Visits are on Sundays from 2 to 5 pm, and each visitor attends an orientation class first. Families can also join Family Recovery, a 9-week course taken together with the residents.

faqs.q: Is work part of the program?
faqs.a: Yes. Residents take part in a work program and daily responsibilities, with training in employment skills and money management. The work has included a maple syrup operation on the property, and the centre says the work builds structure and a work ethic.

Village of Hope talks about accountability partners and long-term connections with its community, and it offers leadership development during the program. A set aftercare schedule is not published. Ask the office what support continues once the 10 months end.

faqs.q: Is Village of Hope a non-profit?
faqs.a: Yes. Village of Hope Inc. is a registered Canadian charity and says it is funded by donations. It operates from the Upper Tracy campus, and a sister Village of Hope runs independently in Estonia.
